## What This Is

**If you run more than one session on your vault, send work to outside models through `external-worker.mjs`, or let your agent use the shell, apply this update.** Four doors had no guard on them. This release puts one on each, with the tests that prove it refuses.

## The Gaps

**The trust-anchor guard watched two tools of four.** It named every Write or Edit to your settings, `CLAUDE.md`, `.mcp.json`, plugins and `.vscode/tasks.json`, and saw nothing an agent did to the same files through the shell. `echo {} > .mcp.json`, `sed -i ... .claude/settings.json` and `Set-Content .claude\CLAUDE.md` all passed it in silence.

**Nothing stopped a sweeping commit.** When two sessions work in one vault, `git add -A` or `git commit -a` in one of them takes the other's unfinished work into its commit, under its message. The coordination script warns that a sibling is active; nothing refused the sweep itself.

**Nothing asked before a git command that throws work away.** The settings carry no ask rule for `git branch -D`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean -f` or a forced push, and a rule matched on text would miss `git -C dir branch --delete --force` anyway.

**The external worker sent whatever it was given.** A context pack from a partner's folder, a prompt naming a partner, an email address or a key-shaped string all went to an outside provider. On a fresh clone the worker also stopped at import when `.env` was missing, before it could say which key it needed.

**A skill with no tier was filed by guess.** The Skills Index builder filled a missing tier from the old index or defaulted it to operational. Four shipped skills carried no tier.

## The Fix

**The trust-anchor guard reads Bash and PowerShell.** A new module, `floor-guard-shell.mjs`, reads a shell command and names every trust anchor it writes, moves, copies onto or deletes: redirects, `sed -i`, `perl -i`, `tee`, `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, `install`, `truncate`, `dd of=`, `git rm`, `git checkout` and `git restore` on a path, interpreter writes (`writeFileSync`, `open(..., "w")`), and PowerShell's `Set-Content`, `Add-Content`, `Out-File`, `Copy-Item`, `Move-Item`, `Remove-Item`, `Rename-Item`, their aliases and `.NET` file writes. An `rm` or `mv` of `.claude`, `.claude/plugins` or `.vscode` counts, since it takes the files inside. Variables assigned earlier in the same command, `$HOME`, `$env:USERPROFILE` and a `cd` are followed. When node cannot run, a by-name match still names the call and says it did not parse. It still surfaces and never blocks. Its registration widens to `Write|Edit|Bash|PowerShell`.

**A sweeping commit in your vault is refused.** `pre-bash-git-add-guard.sh` refuses `git add -A`, `--all`, `.`, `-u` with no path, and `git commit -a`, `-am` or `--all`, when the command runs in your vault (the session's folder, a `cd` into it or `git -C` pointing at it), and names the pathspec form to use instead. Any other repo passes. A heredoc or here-string message that only mentions the words passes. Your vault is `SOVEREIGN_VAULT_ROOT`, or the folder the script shipped in. A folder built from a variable is followed through the command's own assignments and your environment; one it still cannot read asks instead of refusing.

**A destructive git command asks first.** `pre-shell-git-verb-gate.sh` reads the command as tokens, so the spelling stops mattering: `branch -D` or a delete with a force in any order (`-fd`, `--delete --force`), `reset --hard` anywhere, `clean` with a force unless it is a dry run, `update-ref -d`, a push that forces, mirrors, prunes or deletes (including a `+` or `:` refspec), `reflog expire` and `gc --prune`. Global options before the verb are skipped, and `bash -c` and `powershell -Command` are read one level in. It asks and never refuses: these acts are sometimes exactly what you want.

Both git guards fail closed like the Outward Gate: a payload they cannot read, an error or a missing node holds the call. Write and Edit are never matched, so a broken guard leaves the door to repair it.

**Outside models refuse partner material.** `client-material-guard.mjs` refuses a context pack under `Collaborations/` and any text carrying a partner's full name: each folder directly under `Collaborations/` whose name holds a space. Add folders and names in `Council Chamber/scripts/client-material.config.json` (an example ships beside it); a config that does not parse refuses rather than falling back. There is no override. Then a redaction gate stops email addresses, card-like digit runs, payment ids, key-shaped strings and long encoded blobs, naming the class and never the value; `--allow-sensitive` passes with a warning and a logged line. Both run before the key check, and the worker reads a missing `.env` as "no keys yet" rather than stopping.

**The Skills Index refuses a missing tier.** `build-skills-index.mjs` stops with every untiered skill named and writes nothing, in both modes. The index hook now says that refusal to your agent beside the write, rather than only logging it, and rebuilds from the vault root when the session sits in a subfolder. PR Code Review (operational), Pending Plan Progress Update, Quest Progress Update and Source Harvest (foundational) gained their tier; Source Harvest moves from operational in the index to foundational, the tier its source vault gives it.

**The tests.** Every new case was watched failing on v3.24.0 first.

- `hooks-selftest.mjs` grows from 91 to 307 behavior cases and from 16 to 21 registration rows: 131 new trust-anchor cases, 41 for the git-add guard, 40 for the git-verb gate and 4 for the index refusal, plus a wiring row for each shell-reading guard. Against v3.24.0 every new case that demands a reaction fails. Against this release: `behavior: pass=307 fail=0 registration: pass=21 fail=0`, negative control `falsifiable=208 correctly_falsified=208 vacuous=0`.
- `client-material-guard-selftest.mjs` is new, with a CI step of its own: 63 cases on a fixture vault with no provider key, covering refusals, permits, the rules emptied, broken configs, the five redaction classes and the worker refusing for real. Against the v3.24.0 worker its wiring and redaction cases fail. Against this release: `63 ok, 0 failed`.

## If You Are Updating an Existing Vault

1. **Apply the manifest first, then check.** `node "Council Chamber/scripts/se-update.mjs" --apply "Council Chamber/scripts/framework-manifest.json"`, then `--check`. Before the manifest, eight of the new files read as user paths and `--apply` would refuse them. After it, expect 23 framework files and 5 seeded files, with no user paths.
2. **Apply the framework files:** `--apply "<path>"` for each framework file it lists.
3. **The five seeded files, by review.** If you never edited one, apply it with `--force-seeded "<path>"`. Two of them are new (`pre-bash-git-add-guard.sh` and `pre-shell-git-verb-gate.sh`), so `--force-seeded` simply adds them. If you edited `.claude/settings.json`, make two changes by hand in `hooks.PreToolUse`: change the trust-anchor guard's matcher from `"Write|Edit"` to `"Write|Edit|Bash|PowerShell"`, and add these two entries to the `"Bash|PowerShell"` group, each with `"onFailure": "block"`:
   - `"SOVEREIGN_VAULT_ROOT=\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\" bash \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/pre-bash-git-add-guard.sh\""`
   - `"SOVEREIGN_VAULT_ROOT=\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\" bash \"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/pre-shell-git-verb-gate.sh\""`
   If you edited `pre-write-floor-guard.sh` or `post-write-index-regen.sh`, use the spec in step 7.
4. **Commit, then check again.** It should read "Your vault is up to date with upstream."
5. **Rebuild the Skills Index:** `node "Council Chamber/scripts/build-skills-index.mjs" --check`. If it names skills of your own, add `tier: foundational` or `tier: operational` to each one's frontmatter and run it without `--check`.
6. **Fire the positive controls:** `node "Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/hooks-selftest.mjs"` (it takes a few minutes), the same with `--negative-control`, `node "Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/floor-gate-selftest.mjs"` and `node "Council Chamber/scripts/client-material-guard-selftest.mjs"`. Expect zero failures and `vacuous=0`.
7. **If your agent has customized these files**, hand it this spec rather than the diff. The trust-anchor guard sends a Bash or PowerShell payload to `floor-guard-shell.mjs` and turns each hit into the same message, stderr line and log line as a Write hit; when the module cannot answer, it greps the raw payload for `.claude`, `.mcp.json` or `.vscode` and surfaces the call as unparsed. The git-add guard refuses the sweeps listed above only when the resolved folder is inside the vault, and asks when the folder cannot be resolved. The git-verb gate asks on the verbs listed above in any spelling. The external worker runs the path check, the name check and the redaction gate, in that order, before the key check. The index builder refuses a tier other than foundational or operational; the index hook runs it from the vault root and passes its refusal to the agent through `emit-context.mjs`. The tests named above are the acceptance suite. The recipient owns the code. This file owns the standard.

This path was walked on a fresh clone at v3.24.0 against a snapshot of this release: before the manifest the check listed 17 framework, 3 seeded and 8 user paths; after it, 23 framework, 5 seeded and 0 user paths; all 28 applied, none refused; after the commit the clone read "up to date" and matched the release; inside it the hooks read `pass=307 fail=0` and `pass=21 fail=0`, the floor gate `pass=101 fail=0`, the client-material suite 63 of 63 and the Skills Index check in sync.

## What Stays Open

The trust-anchor guard cannot see a path built at run time (a loop, `find -exec`, `Join-Path`, a script written now and run later); its module's header lists each. The git guards read one shell level in, so a git command run from inside a script you call is beyond them. The partner-name check catches a full name and not a description of the person.

## Prerequisites

v3.24.0. Node on PATH, as the README requires. Claude Code 2.1.295 or later.

## Optional?

No. A fence with a gate on two of its four sides keeps nothing in.
